messages:
maria: Quick sync — we're starting work on tenant-specific observability dashboards. Goal: show per-org SLOs + noisy-neighbor signals without leaking PII. Need runtime + infra metric contract and a short onboarding checklist. Who owns which fields?

alex: I can take runtime telemetry contract. Initial list from runtime side: request_rate_per_org, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_generated_per_request, kv_cache_hit_rate, active_streams, model_variant. Need org_id (hashed) and route name.

jin: Infra can provide host-level and cluster-level signals: gpu_util_pct, memory_pressure_pct, node_p99_cpu, queue_depth, pending_work_items, pod_restarts. We'll emit zone and pool tags so console can filter by region.

tara: Console requirements: per-tenant time-series, heatmap for noisy neighbors (correlate gpu_util vs requests), ability to pin alerts to an org and mute/annotate, and a quick rollout toggle to switch from per-tenant to aggregated view. Also need CSV export and permalink. UI will accept tags: org_id, model_variant, region, route.

kevin: Two privacy/security q's: 1) hashing: plan to use sha256(org_id + salt) with salt rotated monthly? 2) sampling: do we send full payload for all tenants or sample traces for high-cardinality fields? Ops oncall needs full p95/p99 always.

maria: For hashing let's use HMAC-SHA256 with org-level salt stored in KMS, rotated quarterly. Sampling: default telemetry sampling = 10% for verbose logs, but we'll force full ingest for any tenant with active alerts or SLO breaches. We'll document exceptions.

alex: Small note on schema: include these runtime tags in every telemetry event: "org_hash", "route", "model_variant", "seq_len", "batch_size". Also add "fallback_used" boolean for routing fallbacks so we can correlate degraded latency with fallbacks. Example event payload below: 

```json
{"org_hash":"<hmac>", "route":"generation.v1", "model_variant":"redwood-3b-q4", "p95_latency_ms":342, "tokens_generated":128, "kv_cache_hit_rate":0.67, "fallback_used":false, "seq_len":512, "batch_size":16}
```

jin: We'll include cluster tags as flat strings and add a numeric "node_allocations" metric for tenant-to-node affinity. Also we can emit a derived metric "noise_index" computed at infra: weighted combination of gpu_util, queue_depth, and memory_pressure. We'll publish the formula in the contract.

tara: UX for noisy neighbor: need both a raw metric and a normalized "noise_index" so product can present a score 0-100. Also want a baseline comparison: show a tenant's noise_index vs historical median for that org and vs cohort median.

kevin: Alerting: want default alert thresholds for noise_index > 75 for 5m and sustained p95 increase > 30% vs baseline. Who owns alert rule defaults?

maria: Ops & platform should agree. Jin propose defaults, platform approves, product can iterate. Action: jin to draft infra formula + defaults, alex to add runtime fields to telemetry, tara to mock console widgets. I'll create a spec doc and ticket.

ops-bot: Created ticket PLAT-4829: "Tenant observability contract + dashboard kickoff" assigned to maria, jin, alex, tara. Due 2026-03-12.

alex: One more: to reduce cardinality, we'll restrict high-cardinality tags (like prompt_id) from metric ingestion — keep them only in sampled logs/traces. We'll expose a correlate-by example tool that links from dashboard to sampled traces.

jin: Agreed. Also we'll expose a per-tenant quota usage metric (tokens consumed / commit) so commercial can debug noisy customers. That will be numeric and updated every minute.

tara: For rollout UX: console needs a canary mode to surface tenant dashboard only for a subset of orgs. We'll add a "dashboard_enabled" flag in tenant metadata that the UI queries. Who manages that flag?

maria: Customer success owns the enablement flow, but platform will expose an admin API to flip the flag. Action: alex to spec admin API (POST /admin/tenants/{org_hash}/dashboard: {enabled:true}).

kevin: I'll take on oncall playbook updates: include steps for detecting noisy neighbor via noise_index, steps to trigger capacity burst or migrate tenant to dedicated pool.

maria: Summary & next steps: 1) jin: draft infra metric formula + defaults (due EOD 1958140800) 2) alex: telemetry schema PR & admin API spec (due in 3 days) 3) tara: console mockups + canary UX (due in 5 days) 4) kevin: update oncall playbook (in 1 week). I'll assemble the spec doc and link tickets. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

alex: I'll open the telemetry PR tonight and ping infra for schema review.

jin: Starting draft now. will post formula here when ready.

tara: Adding mocks to figma and will link here when done.

kevin: Noted. will add runbook steps and test cases.

maria: Closing loop — we'll demo at next platform sync.
